lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p11 - Listen, point and say.

details: Listen, point and say checks understanding of word meaning and sound. Listen and point shows they match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing, clear sounds, and confident repetition.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

details: Point and match gives students controlled practice identifying the target language and strengthens connections between the words and the pictures that represent them.
Look for accurate identification of the target language, and correct matching of the  items in the picture dictionary strips to the same items in the main scene.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p59 - Draw the face.

details: Draw the face strengthens awareness of the parts of the face and gives students an opportunity to practise their fine motor skills.
Look for correct pencil grip, and students including all the missing parts of the face (eyes, ears, nose, and mouth).

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p11 - Say the chant and point to your face.

details: Say the chant strengthens retention of the target language and helps improve pronunciation and stress.
Look for correct stress, confident participation, with most students able to join in with at least the most repeated parts of the chant and some of the TPR actions.
